chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Sa'd al-Askaf, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I was given the long Chapters in place of the Torah, and I was given the Hundred [Verses] in place of the Gospel, and I was given the Doubles in place of the Psalms, and I was preferred with the Detailed [Surahs], sixty-eight Chapters, and they are predominant over the other Books; and the Torah is for Moses, and the Gospel for Jesus, and the Psalms for David.'

key_terms.السُّوَرَ الطِّوَالَ: The long chapters of the Quran
key_terms.الْمَثَانِيَ: The Doubles, referring to Surah Al-Fatiha
key_terms.الْمِئِينَ: The Hundred [Verses], referring to Surah Hud or similar

ai.seo_question: What Quranic chapters replaced the Torah, Gospel, and Psalms according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi outlines the divine gifts of specific Quranic chapters to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) as replacements for the scriptures given to previous prophets. It identifies the long chapters, the hundred-verse chapter, the doubles, and the detailed sixty-eight chapters as superior and comprehensive replacements for the Torah, Gospel, and Psalms respectively. In Shia scholarship, this is often interpreted through the lens of *Tahrim* (preservation) and *Tafsir* (exegesis), where the Quran serves as the *Muhaymin* (guardian/verifier) over previous texts, confirming their original truth while correcting later alterations.
